episode_title: From AI Assistants to AI Coworkers: The Future of Enterprise AIOps | Dr. Rahul Ghodke (CGI)

real_qa.q: Why is building only the AI brain for DevOps insufficient without proper arms and legs in infrastructure?
real_qa.r: Everyone is building the AI brain for DevOps, but nobody is building the arms and legs it needs. A bunch of tools and MCPs doesn't really cut it. The infrastructure and tooling underneath needs to support autonomous operations, as evidenced by incidents where tools like CloudCode have destroyed production databases.
real_qa.requete: AI brain DevOps arms legs MCPs tools

real_qa.q: What is the difference between AI-assisted operations and truly agentic operations in DevOps?
real_qa.r: AI-assisted operations like co-pilots and ChatGPT help individual engineers write code or terraform scripts, but the output depends on who is prompting and their style. True agentic operations require AI to act like a co-worker, standardized and repeatable, not susceptible to individual styles. The shift requires standardized, structured, and repeatable processes with proper governance and context management.
real_qa.requete: AI assistant versus agentic DevOps operations

real_qa.q: How should enterprises choose between classical AI and generative AI for operations management?
real_qa.r: The decision depends on two factors: business economics and workload classification. If a business has limited budget and analytical needs, classical AI may fit better for purpose. For complex processing requiring millisecond-level correlations across event streams impacting millions of users, generative frameworks can justify the cost. However, classical AI can partially solve problems but requires time, effort, and skilled individuals. At CGI, front office event teams are deflected onto machine learning frameworks first, with generative AI invoked only based on issue criticality.
real_qa.requete: classical AI versus generative AI operations management

real_qa.q: What are the main challenges enterprises face when migrating to cloud and how does AI help address them?
real_qa.r: A lot of migrations are today politically challenged and depend upon application owner convenience. Many lift-and-shift migrations from 2019-2020 have resulted in significant cost escalation. CGI uses a factory-based approach with proprietary tools and automation native to migrations, employing close to 3,000 certified SMEs across AWS, Azure, GCP, OCI and others. The company helps customers simplify costs by analyzing every compute and service, balancing reserved instances and spot instances, and ensuring cost optimization and well-architected approaches.
real_qa.requete: cloud migration challenges cost escalation AI optimization

real_qa.q: How do AI agents overcome the amnesia problem of starting without context in enterprise operations?
real_qa.r: AI agents wake up with amnesia every session and don't retain all the information and context required to solve problems at hand. This mirrors the challenge of new team members who lack tribal knowledge. The solution requires making knowledge discoverable, mined, and indexed in a relevant manner through platforms, governance, and skilled teams. Proper cataloging of information and structured presentation to agents significantly improves efficiency and predictability, combined with human-in-the-loop checkpoints where agents stop, review themselves, ask questions, and only proceed after validation.
real_qa.requete: AI agent amnesia context management tribal knowledge

real_qa.q: What percentage of front office automation does AIOps currently cover in enterprise environments?
real_qa.r: AIOps is very limited to only 10-20% of the front office automation in enterprises. This indicates that while AI operations are advancing, the majority of automation still relies on classical approaches and manual processes, suggesting significant room for agentic frameworks and hybrid intelligence models to expand coverage.
real_qa.requete: AIOps front office automation coverage percentage
